cases.prompt: Our app throws CannotGetJdbcConnectionException after 3 seconds and p99 is 8 seconds. Should we raise the pool size?
expectations: Treats pool wait as a symptom and asks what the queries are doing
Checks database CPU and session count before proposing a pool change
Insists on the slow statement and its plan before any sizing change
Orders the diagnosis steps numerically with before-and-after percentiles

cases.prompt: Page 10000 of invoices takes 6 seconds. Page 1 is fast. Fix it.
expectations: Explains that OFFSET makes the database read and discard the skipped rows
Proposes keyset pagination with the full sort key including the tiebreaker
States the tradeoff that keyset loses numbered page jumps and needs a cursor
Requires the cursor to be opaque and the composite index to match filter then sort

cases.prompt: Every page load runs SELECT count(*) on a 40 million row invoices table.
expectations: Rejects a full count per request and distinguishes it from an existence check
Proposes SELECT 1 LIMIT 1 for existence and a cached or approximate total for pagination
Warns that pg_class.reltuples is only as fresh as the last ANALYZE
Rejects the count for any billing or compliance figure

cases.prompt: This query is 4 ms on my laptop with 2000 rows. Why is it 900 ms in production?
expectations: Rejects the dev measurement as invalid evidence
Lists row count, skew, cache state, storage, and concurrency as the differences to reproduce
Requires a production-like data load with a distribution and a fresh ANALYZE
Notes the plan chosen for a small table is legitimately a sequential scan

cases.prompt: Should we raise hibernate.jdbc.batch_size from 50 to 5000 to speed up our imports?
expectations: Treats batch size as a memory and lock trade rather than a bigger-is-better dial
Requires measurement at multiple sizes such as 10, 50, and 200
Checks that the identifier strategy permits batching at all
Warns that a large batch holds more rows and locks inside a single statement

cases.prompt: We added an index and the EXPLAIN looks much better. Can we close the ticket?
expectations: Rejects a plan change as proof of an improvement
Requires before-and-after p50, p95, and p99 on the same workload and data volume
Requires a regression guard such as a statement count assertion or a perf budget
Requires a revert plan if the metric does not move
